name: Ichor
baseline: Boost.Beast (pure Beast http_server_fast-style server, beast_benchmark in the same repo)
workload: wrk POST of a small JSON body ({"sequence": 2}) to /ping on a localhost echo-style server, at 2, 400 and 20,000 connections, comparing Ichor's pong example (HTTP service layered on Boost.Beast) with a hand-written pure Boost.Beast server.
claimed_speedup: Requests/sec Ichor + Boost.Beast vs pure Boost.Beast: 67,194.72 vs 41,397.00 at 2 connections (about 1.6x, derived from page data); 87,048.80 vs 73,975.13 at 400 connections (about 1.18x, derived from page data); 72,971.55 vs 37,311.37 at 20,000 connections (about 1.96x, derived from page data). Page also lists Drogon at 132,285.77 / 132,936.53 / 117,676.17 and Go fasthttp at 165,747.41 / 170,028.45 / 123,741.19 requests/s, both faster than Ichor.
compiler_and_flags: Ichor built with cmake -GNinja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DICHOR_ARCH_OPTIMIZATION=X86_64_AVX2 -DICHOR_USE_BOOST_BEAST=ON -DICHOR_USE_SANITIZERS=OFF; README setup line lists gcc 13.1.1 and clang 18 but does not say which compiled the HTTP runs; build flags of the pure Beast server are not stated.
hardware: AMD 7950X, 6000MHz CL38 RAM, Ubuntu 22.04 (stated at the top of the benchmarks README for the preliminary results; not restated in the HTTP section).
tradeoffs: C++20 framework (event queue, coroutines, dependency injection); the HTTP path is Boost.Beast underneath, HTTPS only through Beast, partial HTTP/1.1 implementation. The README says Ichor 'cheats' by running user logic on a separate thread from the networking thread while the other servers did everything on one thread. Service creation with dependencies is likely O(N^2) and uses a lot of memory per its own conclusions.
caveats: First-party numbers. The baseline is Ichor's own foundation (Boost.Beast), not the libevent or Asio baselines guessed for the category. The pure Beast rows all show wrk socket read errors (418,099 / 740,671 / 374,703 read errors in the 2, 400 and 20,000 connection runs), so the baseline throughput may be partly failed requests. Ichor runs lasted 60 s and Beast runs 10 s. The README says the benchmarks identify bottlenecks and do not showcase performance; proper throughput and latency benchmarks are TBD. Drogon and Go fasthttp are 1.5x to 2.5x faster than Ichor on the same page. Ichor's README goal is only 'performance matching at least Boost Beast'. Hardware, compiler and flags are not stated for the HTTP section specifically.
